rv.q: Until then, she and her human co-stars provide a late summer afternoon’s dream.
A worthwhile revival of a rarely performed Shakespeare, proving once and for all that ‘love and a bit with a dog’ really is what the people want.
Somewhat laboured comedy enlivened by a warm, all-male cast...
However, regrettably there was so much that was wrong with this production that it failed to spark any interest in the plot, and those 90 minutes or so felt interminably long.

cn.t: This pacy, music-filled RSC production aimed at younger audiences wins praise for its accessible approach and scene-stealing dog, though critics remain divided on whether it fully succeeds as a gateway to Shakespeare's lesser-known early work.
